title: Tool protocol is the open-core license boundary
context: OpenKaava is open core: Apache-licensed shell, proprietary first-party tools, one public protocol. Each repository (first-party, commercial, third-party) is built against the tool protocol.
decision: The tool protocol (`docs/tool-protocol.md`) is the contract the entire model rests on. Nothing crosses this boundary. A change that reaches around it—a private tool poking at orchestrator internals, or the orchestrator growing a special case for one tool—is declined on principle rather than on quality, including when the code is good.
consequences: When something genuinely needs more from the other side, there are two moves and no third: generalize it so any tool could want it and land it in core, or accept that it belongs in the tool. No special cases are allowed. This prevents open-core rot but requires discipline.
